source_refs.note: Exercise 6.5, Question 18 (book page 211); answer key PDF 308.

blocks.prompt: 18. A hyperbola for which \(a = b\) is called rectangular. Show that a hyperbola is rectangular if and only if its asymptotes are perpendicular to one another.
blocks.explanation:
"If and only if" (agar aur sirf agar) ka matlab hai ke humein do baatein saabit karni hain: (1) rectangular ho to asymptotes perpendicular hon, aur (2) asymptotes perpendicular hon to hyperbola rectangular ho.
Dono baatein ek hi cheez se nikalti hain: asymptotes ke slopes ka product \(-\frac{b^2}{a^2}\) hai.
Rule kaunsa? Perpendicular lines ke slopes ka product \(-1\).
Plan: pehle yeh product nikalenge, phir dono taraf ka saboot (proof) alag alag likhenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) (\(a, b > 0\)); rectangular ka matlab \(a = b\).
Saabit karna: \(a = b\) tab aur sirf tab jab asymptotes perpendicular hon.
Tareeqa: Kitab ke asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x\) aur perpendicular lines ki shart \(m_1 m_2 = -1\) ko dono simton (directions) mein istemal karenge. Pehle "agar rectangular to perpendicular", phir ulti taraf "agar perpendicular to rectangular".

Asymptotes ke slopes ka product
\[m_1 = \dfrac{b}{a},\quad m_2 = -\dfrac{b}{a}\]
\[m_1 m_2 = -\dfrac{b^2}{a^2}\]
Kyun: Kitab (Figure 6.23) mein is hyperbola ke asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x\) hain. Dono mein se koi bhi vertical nahi, is liye slopes wala test lag sakta hai. Plus aur minus ka product minus deta hai, is liye \(-\frac{b^2}{a^2}\).

Hissa 1: rectangular \(\Rightarrow\) perpendicular
\[a = b\]
\[m_1 m_2 = -\dfrac{a^2}{a^2} = -1\]
Kyun: Rectangular hyperbola mein \(b = a\) hota hai, to product mein \(b\) ki jagah \(a\) rakha. Product \(-1\) aaya, aur yahi perpendicular lines ki pehchan hai.

Hissa 2: perpendicular \(\Rightarrow\) rectangular
\[m_1 m_2 = -1\]
\[-\dfrac{b^2}{a^2} = -1\]
\[b^2 = a^2\]
\[b = a\]
Kyun: Ab ulta chal rahe hain: maan liya ke asymptotes perpendicular hain, to product \(-1\) hoga. Dono taraf se minus hataya aur \(a^2\) se multiply kiya. \(a\) aur \(b\) lengths hain, dono positive, is liye \(b^2 = a^2\) se \(b = a\) hi nikalta hai (\(b = -a\) mumkin nahi). Yani hyperbola rectangular hai.
Dhyan dein: Sirf ek taraf saabit karna adhoora jawab hai; "if and only if" mein dono hisse likhna zaroori hain.

Baaqi shaklein
\[\dfrac{y^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{x^2}{b^2} = 1:\quad m_1 m_2 = -\dfrac{a^2}{b^2}\]
Kyun: Vertical hyperbola ke asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{a}{b}x\) hote hain; phir bhi product \(-1\) tab hi hota hai jab \(a = b\). Agar centre \((h, k)\) par chala jaye to asymptotes sirf khisak jate hain, un ke slopes nahi badalte. Is liye yeh nateeja har hyperbola par lagta hai.

Tasdeeq misaal se
\[x^2 - y^2 = 4:\quad y = \pm x\]
\[(1)(-1) = -1\;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Is misaal mein \(a = b = 2\) hai aur asymptotes \(y = x\) aur \(y = -x\) hain, jo 45 degree aur 135 degree par hain, yani aapas mein 90 degree. Kitab ke note mein bhi yahi likha hai ke rectangular hyperbola ke asymptotes perpendicular hote hain. Figure mein right angle ka nishaan dekhiye.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: asymptotes ke slopes ka product \(-\frac{b^2}{a^2}\) hai, jo \(-1\) tab aur sirf tab hota hai jab \(a = b\). Yani hyperbola rectangular hai agar aur sirf agar us ke asymptotes perpendicular hon.
